issue.title: [Epic] Audio recording & playback (Expo modules)
issue.body:
### Summary

Epic tracking audio recording & playback on the **Expo SDK 56 CNG (Android-only) baseline**. The audio feature is **genuinely net-new** on this baseline — `ViewChapter.tsx` currently has only a **mock record/playback toggle** (`VerseState = 'idle' | 'recording' | 'recorded'`, no files). Build it on first-party Expo modules: **`expo-audio`** + **`expo-file-system`**. The junior handoff [PR #82](https://github.com/eten-tech-foundation/fluent-mobile/pull/82) (Simform waveform + `react-native-fs`) is **not merging** and is referenced only as anti-patterns.

**Verify pass (2026-07):** All sub-issues still open — net-new feature work. Recordings join in `queries.ts` already uses `bible_text_id` on main; remaining #98 scope is multi-take wiring and persistence.

What already exists on main to build against:
- `recordings` table with `local_file_path`, `take_number`, `is_latest`, `duration_ms`, `file_size_bytes`, `sync_status` (#94, #98).
- `queries.ts` recordings join on `bible_text_id` (was incorrectly `chapter_assignment_id`; fixed on main).

### Sub-issues
- [x] #94
- [x] #95
- [x] #96
- [x] #97
- [x] #98

### Dependency ordering
1. **#94** (`expo-file-system` storage) — foundation; id-based paths.
2. **#95** (`expo-audio` recorder) and **#96** (`expo-audio` playback + waveform decision) — engines.
3. **#97** (testable state machine) composes #94/#95/#96.
4. **#98** (multi-take wiring + persistence) — coordinate with C1 (#99).
- F3 (#111) provides jest mocks for `expo-audio`/`expo-file-system`.
- B must land before C (upload, epic #117) since the upload worker reads the latest pending recording.

### Links
- Anti-pattern reference only (not merging): [PR #82](https://github.com/eten-tech-foundation/fluent-mobile/pull/82)

comments.body:
Closing as completed (tracker cleanup after repo audit).

All epic sub-issues are done and closed: #94, #95, #96, #97, #98. Recording/playback on Expo modules is on `main` (engines + Record tab). Follow-ups like multi-take UI (#71) and source-audio dock (#235) are tracked separately.
